daily_quests.title: ASX 200 Daily Returns & Ranking
daily_quests.description: Using ASX 200 historical price data, calculate the daily percentage return for each stock. Use a window function (ROW_NUMBER or RANK) to rank stocks by return within each trading date, partitioned by date. Then use a CTE to identify the top 5 and bottom 5 performers for each date. Return: date, stock_symbol, close_price, daily_return_pct, rank_within_date. Filter for the last 30 trading days only.

daily_quests.title: NSW Road Crash Data Cleaning & Risk Scoring
daily_quests.description: Download NSW Road Crash data (CSV format). Clean the dataset by: (1) removing rows with missing critical fields (crash_date, latitude, longitude, severity); (2) standardising date formats to YYYY-MM-DD; (3) handling inconsistent severity labels (map variations to standard categories: Fatal, Serious Injury, Other Injury); (4) removing duplicate records based on crash_id; (5) calculating a risk_score (1-10) based on severity and number of vehicles involved. Export the cleaned dataset to a new CSV with all original columns plus risk_score. Provide a data quality report (rows removed, % missing values before/after).

daily_quests.title: Australian Weather Anomalies: Python ETL → SQL Analysis
daily_quests.description: Step 1 (Python): Download Australian Weather observations dataset (temperature, rainfall, humidity by station/date). Use pandas to: clean missing values, convert all temperatures to Celsius, filter for the last 12 months, calculate rolling 7-day average temperature and total rainfall by station. Export to CSV. Step 2 (SQL): Load the cleaned CSV into a database. Write a query using window functions (LAG, LEAD) to identify temperature anomalies: flag any day where the temperature deviation from the 7-day rolling average exceeds 2 standard deviations. Return: station_name, date, temp, rolling_avg, deviation_std, is_anomaly (boolean). Include the top 10 stations with the most anomalies.
